notes.title: Friendly Update
notes.content:
[h2]Greetings, Raid Leaders![/h2]

This update is friendly. Not friendly enough to dub it "welcoming" - but hey, it's less hostile than the others!

As Steam's Endless Replayability Fest kicks off, let's get into what's new!

[h3]ːsteamthumbsupː Improved Game Start UI and Hints[/h3]
If you've been sticking around for a while - well, you probably don't need all that. But new players still do! Your suffering haven't been in vain, because it would be easier for people to get into the game and actually understand what's happening.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43947105/e898f3bebf4f5c0b43ab4fa670ffaafdd0527f67.png[/img]
Well, at least I hope so! Do you agree? Tell me what you think!

[h3]Tech & Oprimization[/h3]
The game has been upgraded to the new tech! It now runs Unreal Engine 5.4 under the hood - instead of the old 5.2. The game looks better than ever and runs much smoother than it used to. 
I hope this makes the experience more enjoyable for you!

[h3]Updated Music[/h3]
The amazing [url=https://twitter.com/phyrnna]@Phyrnna[/url] has created an incredibly catchy track, which can now be heard while fighting especially menacing foes like Captain Slimebeard.
Fighting a slimy crab pirate who slings barrels of rum around have never been so epic!
In the meantime, check out Phyrnna's other work. You'll agree with me she's great.


Improvements marked with ːsteamthumbsupː were based on the feedback I got from all of you so far. Keep it coming!

As always - I'll be happy to see you on Crab Raid Tactics Discord, hear your honest thoughts and awesome ideas!

[url=https://discord.gg/rqx9Ne8kF4][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43947105/080cb9a2298e7a002c6e6a5eab38df71cf8ac924.png[/img][/url]

GL;HF!
[i][b]Stefan, Your Dungeon Master[/b][/i]

notes.title: Stolen Update
notes.content:
[h2]Greetings, Raid Leaders![/h2]

Another event is coming - this time, it is DevGAMM Gdansk! If any of you plan to attend - I will be there, showcasing the game at the booth A9 on both days, so come say 'Hi!"

While I prepare bigger changes and additions to the game, now's the time to apply a little polish!
Here's what's new:

[h2]Kleptoslimes[/h2]
What? Yes!
Did you think that you could just leave all those treasures lying around, knowing that all of that becomes yours by the end of the battle? This is no longer the case, as greedy crustaceans finally get some competition. If you decide to take your time collecting your hard-earned Loot, the pesky little Kleptoslimes will appear and try to steal it from you. Catch them before they flee!
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43947105/fc7e1415a077a24a1a808407b0017e3dededb238.gif[/img]

[h2]All changes[/h2]

[h3]Gameplay & Balance[/h3]
[list]
[*] New conditional event: Kleptoslimes
[*] Updated Shine reaction mechanics to work more consistently
[*] Updated Glitter Smite to grant extra loot more consistently
[*] Updated Storm reaction visuals & buffed it significantly, to make it more noticeable & comparable in power to other reactions
[*] Added short (0.5 second) damage immunity for all monsters when they spawn
[*] Fixed issues with capture points in Treasure Hunt - used to progress slower then intended when monsters were present on the point
[*] Slightly increased Loot Magnet size for all crabs
[*] Fixed a bug with Level Up options not updating after receiving a Trinket from an Elemental Favor
[*]  ːsteamthumbsupː Urchin Traps & WIther Fairies take longer to spawn
[*]  ːsteamthumbsupː Loot Drops no longer get stuck after the battle is over
[/list]

[h3]Graphics[/h3]
[list]
[*] Updated lighting on all scenes once again. Tell me if you like it more!
[*] Added outlines to crabs
[*] Added highlight for crabs that are behind opaque objects
[/list]

[h3]UI/UX[/h3]
[list]
[*] Introduced graphical cursor
[*] ːsteamthumbsupː Added Codex to in-game menu
[*] ːsteamthumbsupː Added health indication for Totems (green to red glow underneath the totem)
[*] ːsteamthumbsupː Improved telegraphing for Wither Fairies in Brinebough Forest
[*] ːsteamthumbsupː Improved telegraphing for Urchin Traps in Shallow Reef

[*] ːsteamthumbsupː Added a "?" sign to Next Encounter Info widget to indicate it's clickable
[/list]

Improvements marked with ːsteamthumbsupː were based on the feedback I got from all of you so far. Keep it coming!

notes.title: Rewarding Update
notes.content:
[h2]Merry Christmas and Happy New Year, Raid Leaders![/h2]

302 days ago, in March, Crab Raid Tactics demo have been published on Itch. Later, in May, it came to Steam as well. I want to sincerely thank everyone who played the game, added it to their wishlist, shared their feedback and ideas with me. When this game finally matures enough to be released - that would be thanks to all of you.

Throughout this year, I applied to several online and offline events, and was able to showcase Crabs on some of them:
[list]
[*] [url=https://itch.io/jam/feedback-quest-3/rate/1916863]Feedback Quest 3 on Itch.io[/url]
[*] [url=https://itch.io/jam/feedback-quest-4/rate/1916863]Feedback Quest 4 on Itch.io - Scored #3-#4 in Graphics and Overall Fun[/url], 4th place
[*] [url=https://itch.io/jam/feedback-quest-5/rate/1916863]Feedback Quest 5 on Itch.io - Scored #1-#3 in every category![/url], 2nd place
[*] Steam Strategy Fest - Store Showcase
[*] [url=https://devgamm.com/lisbon2023/event-highlights/]DevGAMM Lisbon 2023[/url] / IndieX Steam Event
[*] [url=https://devgamm.com/lisbon2023/event-highlights/]DevGAMM Lisbon 2023[/url] Game Showcase
[*] [url=https://devgamm.com/lisbon2023/event-highlights/]DevGAMM Lisbon 2023[/url] Public Pitch (won that one as well)
[/list]
For now, let's celebrate all that with the last update of this year! I have something nice in store for those who've been following the game and providing suggestions

[h2]Objectives and Rewards[/h2]
Remember side objectives added in the last update? With this update, side objectives now give out minor rewards. So far, it is limited to "Loot" and "Pearls", but the expansion of the reward pool is something I'll start working on soon!
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43947105/d853db0a098a3b42942e823cd310d6d921ba2ca3.gif[/img]

The rewards themselves also got a significant facelift, and several graphical artifacts related to them have been fixed.

[h2]UX And QoL Changes[/h2]
Over the course of this year, I've received numerous requests about some things. Always in a hurry, moving from country to country, preparing the build for one even or the other, I wasn't able to give enough love to those things. But I can now!

[h3]Move All Button ːsteamthumbsupː[/h3]
That's right, it's finally here :) there is now a separate button and hotkey to command all three Crabs to move out to the same location. This is the first implementation, so I am sure you would have a lot of comments, requests and ideas about how to make it better. If you do - don't hesitate to let me know!
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43947105/afa1791245b90b655ea1f5bb059e5541600941d7.jpg[/img]

[h3]Settings & Quit buttons in-game ːsteamthumbsupː[/h3]
Any game should have that, that's basic stuff. So, Crab Raid Tactics now has it, too!

[h3]Attunement UIːsteamthumbsupː[/h3]
The UI window for attunement reward now automatically pre-selects a Crab that can attune an ability, instead of always selecting the first Crab in the squad.

[h3]UI improvements ːsteamthumbsupː[/h3]
The overall UI style have been tweaked to improve clarity and readability, and highlight on all the selectable elements have been updated. Also, gradient fonts! Do you like gradient fonts? I like gradient fonts!
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43947105/5225783799d6256680c15985eded12e4d3c70589.jpg[/img]

[h3]Main Menu update[/h3]
Ok, nobody actually asked for it, but I'm kind of proud of this one. Just look at how much it changed!
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43947105/dc4100995bb8feeb975f74d4560bf284e504822b.gif[/img]

[h2]Lighting Update and Performance Options[/h2]
Making the Settings Menu accessible during the run led to a minor rework of all the performance options, so they could be safely changed mid-game. I had to spend extra time to fix some of the existing issues with graphics and performance. There was also another iteration on the lighting on all game scenes - to make Crabs stand out a bit ore on every environment. Let me know if I actually succeeded!


Improvements marked with ːsteamthumbsupː were based on the feedback I got from all of you so far. Keep it coming!

As always - I'll be happy to see you on Crab Raid Tactics Discord, hear your honest thoughts and awesome ideas!

[url=https://discord.gg/rqx9Ne8kF4][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43947105/080cb9a2298e7a002c6e6a5eab38df71cf8ac924.png[/img][/url]

GL;HF! Until the next year!
[i][b]Stefan, Your Dungeon Master[/b][/i]

notes.title: Pathfinder's Update
notes.content:
[h2]Greetings, Raid Leaders![/h2]

You probably haven't heard a lot of things about Crab Raid Tactics, and that's about to change.
I won't bore you with a lot of details about how Ex Tenebris is officially an Indie Studio based in Slovenia, and how I am a proud founder of it. 

Today, I bring you the first update that proudly wears its own name - Pathfinder's Update! 
Today is also the start of Steam Strategy Fest, so would it not be the perfect occasion?

[h2]Raid Structure[/h2]
Remember how levels used to shuffle randomly between Shore and Underwater areas?
Time for some pathfinding to happen. It is now divided into different Areas. There are three, currently:
[list]
[b][*] Sandy Shore
[*] Shallow Reef 
[*] Brinebough Forest (new!)[/b][/list]
Each area has a unique arena mechanic to be aware of.

[b]Sandy Shore[/b] still have those sandy exposions from before, that appear out of nowhere from time to time.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43947105/e9d2033e336223ab2c828d7a9214811ce30b3685.jpg[/img]

[b]Shallow Reef[/b] is invaded by Sea Urchins that don't like to be near Crabs and explode violently when poked
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43947105/8969a7be50d0e1802213843abcbcbff186a606c3.jpg[/img]

[b]Brinebough Forest[/b] has Withering Fairies that don't want any Crabs trampling their verdant lawn.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43947105/08ec46558e23e517791e627cad37e88ac6b8c271.jpg[/img]

Right now, there is only one Arena Event tied to each area. There are plans to add more in the future. For now, those three would be used to clearly state my intention to make every area meaningfully different in terms of challenge. All of them share the same monster set for now, and that is another thing that would probably change in the future.


At the end of each Encounter, when you are choosing the portal, you may now occasionally be offered a passage to another Area, on certain conditions: for example, Sandy Shore is connected to both Brinebough Forest and Shallow Reef, but you can't travel from Reef to Forest directly. While there are only 3 areas available, the plan is to have as much as 8 of them for the release.

[h2]UX Improvements[/h2]

There are many small changes done to the game's UI to make it more understandable and straightforward. Most of it is based on the feedback I got from you! 

[i]Also, no, there is no "Move All" button yet. I know you want it. I admit it is a good idea. I cave in.
I did not have enough time to implement it right now, but I will definitely add it later.[/i]

[h3]Raid Results ːsteamthumbsupː[/h3]
Something to brag about and post in our [url=https://discord.gg/rqx9Ne8kF4]DISCORD SERVER[/url] for everyone to see
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43947105/e74d2863d8627fef1c348fd07911d1e8407e8d1f.jpg[/img]

[h3] Raid Progress [/h3]
Shows the current progress towards the boss, as well as some stats - like passed time or Hostility level (Guess you never knew the game gets harder and harder with each encounter by the power of this hidden parameter, huh? Now it's out there!)
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43947105/fda59d7519821ee3594013bea774ea91902e31a3.jpg[/img]

[h3] Path Information ːsteamthumbsupː[/h3]
A lot of you mentioned it was unclear what those icons in front of portals mean. With this update - there is a way to present that information to give more context to your choise. 
Portal VFX were also changed, and its visuals are now tied to Areas they lead to.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43947105/4bf3c3c32d45a232da7b7ed0c689537f16f15fd9.jpg[/img]

[h3] No Portals until the Reward is picked up ːsteamthumbsupː[/h3]
Paths forward only activates after the reward has been picked up. This has been an issue for a while now, and a lot of players saw it as an issue.

[h3] Graphics for Smite ability ːsteamthumbsupː[/h3]
Smite got its own graphics now and no longer looks the same way Seafoam Slash does - both VFX and icon has been updated for it

[h3] Credits[/h3]
A small, but very important addition - Hall of Fame for everyone who contributed (willingly or unwillingly) to this game's content.

Improvements marked with ːsteamthumbsupː were based on the feedback I got from all of you so far. Keep it coming!

As always - I'll be happy to see you on Crab Raid Tactics Discord, hear your honest thoughts and awesome ideas!

[url=https://discord.gg/rqx9Ne8kF4][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43947105/a77fcbf75854609e0f2e29a52e32e702d2315281.png[/img][/url]

GL;HF! Until the next time!

notes.title: Demo Update: Version 0.6.0.d Release Notes
notes.content:
[h2]Greetings, Raid Leaders![/h2]
The demo hasn't been out for long - it released a month ago here on Steam and about 4 months ago on Itch. Through all of this game's public existence, this update is the biggest one yet. The game has received a ton of improvements based on your feedback, and I am proud to present all the good stuff to you today!

[h2]Elemental Reactions[/h2]
Core gameplay of Crab Raid Tactics has finally received its biggest missing piece - Elemental Reactions become available with this update! If you missed the previous post about it - Reactions are triggered when enemies are attacked with abilities Attuned to different Elements. This adds even more depth to the choise of upgrades, providing another way to optimize your team composition
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43947105/a0ff0c4ce5451f0df4e9cc49dfcc5ac83c3fe45c.gif[/img]
This system would not be complete without a Spirit attribute for crabs, that affects the power of caused reactions. It also provides some alternative to Attack stat, effectively adding another way to increase crab's damage output in the mid and late game.

[h2]Permanent Progression[/h2]
The core loop of a roguelite game could not be complete without Permanent Upgrades - something to look forward to after each run. This upgrade introduces the basic progression system! It does not have a lot of content (and any further content will most probably not be included in the Demo), but it does provide ways of improving your Raid's performance in different ways. 
You won't be, however, able to use all the possible buffs at the same time - each upgrade is focused around a certain aspect of the game and provides two different options of improving it.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43947105/3bdbbb19ad0a54371dd6c3c2d27fee2cbabddf79.gif[/img]
This also helps to improve the experience for players who see the game for the first time, locking some of the complexities behind the progression. For example, Healing Totem, that used to be available right from the beginning, has been changed to be an unlockable random event.

[h2]Complete Rebalance of the whole game[/h2]
The encounter system has been reworked completely. The objectives haven't changed - the goal is still to eliminate all attackers or survive their onslaught, but the way it's done has been significantly improved.
[list]
[*] First of all, the way monsters are selected for the encounter has been changed. Each monster squad that is spawned now has a different enemy composition, allowing for more variety and fun. There is a whole new system in place to ensure the fights are being challenging and fair. 
[*] The amount of monsteres and difficulty of the encounters have been incresed significantly! I was afraid of scaring off new players with difficult gameplay at first, but the game is supposed to be about strategy and tactical decisions. Even the first level is now quite difficult and requires careful planning to complete. And then again, who does not like mowing through hordes of enemies that burst into explosions of shiny trinkets?
[*] Captain Slimebeard, the one and only boss implemented so far, has moved to an encounter #13, and beating him does not end the game. Instead, after this fight all following encounters become significantly harder, giving you an opportunity to put your squad to the ultimate test![/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43947105/bbd61d9f98623e80d5624a7bfccef594a50207ee.gif[/img]

[h2]UX Improvements[/h2]
Even though there is very little content implemented to this moment, Crab Raid Tactics is a pretty compex game at its core. It features a ton of mechanics that are far from obvious - even recently added Elemental Reactions need proper explaination.
The will be a proper tutorial one day, but for now, there is a Codex that contains a lot of useful information on the existing features.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43947105/2246fba29b0fc46973b2456bdc39cd4daf258983.gif[/img]
Apart from that, there are also small, but still very significant improvements - like the hotkey indication near Crabs' healthbars, to make controlling them even easier in the middle of the fight.

[h2]Sounds and Music[/h2]
The gameplay music is coming to the world of Crab Raid Tactics! Thanks to [b]amazing [url=https://phyrnna.carrd.co/]Phyrnna[/url][/b], the game now features an original music track! While it is not yet finalized and there is still a lot left to do, this is a welcome and long-awaited addition many playtesters mentioned before.
This update also introduces a couple of ambient tracks for all locations (brought to you by [url=https://pixabay.com/]Pixabay[/url]), and a number of missing SFX have been added for collecting loot pieces and rewards.

[h2]What's next[/h2]
This update brings the Demo much closer to what it is intended to be. A lot of systems are in place now, and there is (almost) enough content to experience what the game is about

That being said, there's still a number of improvements that need to happen before this demo could be considered complete - it requires balancing, improvements to game flow and UI screens (especially Raid Over UI). I have plans to do some UX improvements and implement a proper tutorial with some narrative elements to it. 
There are also several missing systems of the core gameplay - the biggest one left being Shell Abilities. They are meant as conditional abilities that trigger passively when something happens (picking up Loot or defeating an enemy), or manually triggerable raid-wide buffs with a limited amount of uses per encounter.

The content of the demo is unlikely to change significantly from now on - it will receive most of the freshly-implemented systems with minimal content as an example, but once those things are in place, the main focus would be on polishing, optimizing and producing enough content for an Early Access release, that will have a price tag on it.

As always - I'll be happy to see you on Crab Raid Tactics Discord, hear your honest thoughts and awesome ideas!
[url=https://discord.gg/rqx9Ne8kF4][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43947105/a77fcbf75854609e0f2e29a52e32e702d2315281.png[/img][/url]

GL;HF! Until the next time!
[i][b]Stefan, Your Dungeon Master[/b][/i]

notes.title: Elemental Reactions
notes.content:
[h1]Greetings, Raid Leaders![/h1]
In today's update I will be covering the last missing piece of Crab Raid Tactics' core gameplay - Elemental Reactions! I had this system in mind for a while, but was reluctant to implement it from the start - it does complicate things in the long run, and I wanted to make sure existing core gameplay is polished and comfortable enough to accept a new system on top of it. While there are still improvements to be made - I believe now's the best time to spice it up a bit.

[h1]What are Elemental Reactions?[/h1]
Those of you who are familiar with games like Magicka, Genshin Impact or Divinity series are probably familiar with the concept: mixing different kind of magic produces various new effects, like mixing Water and Fire magic to produce Vapor.

Crabs don't know Fire Magic, though. Their system of beliefs takes its roots in a different things:
[list]
[*][b]Sand[/b] gives them a ground to crawl on
[*][b]Sun[/b] warms them with its light
[*][b]Ocean's[/b] waves keep them cool and healthy
[*][b]Wind[/b] blows over their shells
[*][b]Nature[/b] provides them with food [spoiler][i]Should i call it Algae instead? I should probably call it Algae[/i][/spoiler] 
[*][b]Greed[/b] drives them to gather for a raid and travel further and further away from their cozy village to seek glorious shiny things
[/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43947105/2e59286f8375b17a9f6e3e456b244a11897fa839.png[/img]

Each ability in Crab Raid Tactics already has 5 elemental variants, called Elemental Attunements: one for each element, excluding [b]Nature[/b]. Attuning ability to an element changes it, introducing new mechanics. For example, [b]Ocean[/b] attunement can turn projectiles into waves that push enemies away, while [b]Wind[/b] makes them explode for AoE damage.

With multiple Attuned abilities in place, Reactions become possible. When enemies receive damage from an element - they gain Exposure to that element. Attacking them with another element may cause a reaction, that either empoweres an attack that triggered it or produces a new effect entirely. For example, mixing [b]Ocean[/b] and [b]Sand[/b] together would trigger an Overgrow reaction, converting dealt damage to [b]Nature[/b] element and applying [b]Nature[/b] exposure - which can, in turn, react with [b]Sun[/b] for increased damage, [b]Greed[/b] for Lifesteal or [b]Wind[/b] for [b]Nature[/b]-based AoE explosion.

[previewyoutube=PRpJKK9OvWk;full][/previewyoutube]

Among the elements, there are two exceptions - as mentioned before, [b]Nature[/b] does not have its own ability, relying on the Overgrow reaction, and [b]Wind[/b] does not apply Exposure, being able to trigger reactions only when other Exposures are applied first.

I would not cover every possible reaction here - and there is a total of 8. Rather, I would be happy to let you play with them and see how you -react- to this new addition, once the update is rolled out :)

I hope this system will provide a better variety for the mid-to-late game, making attunements even more important, and different team compositions more valid.
There is another small change that gives extra depth to the progression in general - Reactions are scaled with the newly introduced Spirit parameter, so the Attack is not the only stat that can directly affect the damage output of the team. I covered this in detail on our Discord server - which you should consider joining, if you want to be first to know more about what's happening behind the scenes, or have an awesome idea I should implement into the game! Ideas for some of the best Quality of Life improvements I introduced came from the people who played the game and shared their thoughts with me - that's why I am, as always, looking forward to your feedback!

[url=https://discord.com/invite/rqx9Ne8kF4][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43947105/a77fcbf75854609e0f2e29a52e32e702d2315281.png[/img][/url]

In the next two weeks, permanent progression and balancing will remain my main focus. I hope to roll out a new build with all this stuff by the end of June, and before that there will be another post regarding progression.

Until then - GL,HF!
[i][b]Stefan, Your Dungeon Master[/b][/i]

notes.title: The Demo has launched!
notes.content:
[b]Introduction[/b]
Welcome to Crab Raid Tactics - a unique blend of a Roguelike Dungeon Crawler and a Combat-Oriented Real Time Strategy. 
The idea for this game came to me a long time ago, when I was a Raid Leader in a WoW guild. The boss mechanics there inspired me, and I wanted to make a single-player experience that would capture the feel of leading your squad in battle and helping them overcome boss mechanics while they fool around, struggling to get out of AoE zones.

Crab Raid Tactics has controls of a strategy game. Each unit - a crab - posesses a number of abilities and uses them on cooldown. It is up to the player to position the squad strategically to face the coming challenge. 

Speaking of challenges - apart from monsters, each combat encounter contains a number of Arena Events - environmental effects, both beneficial and harmful. Proper positioning and quick reaction is required to get the most out of them and mitigate potential harm - the same way it would work in any MMORPG raid, where every player has to pay attention to their surroundings, avoid incoming damage and use unique encounter mechanics to beat the boss.

[b]Developer[/b]
My name is Stefan. Hi! I've been working in gamedev for about 8 years. My trade skill is programming, but I've also been involved in Game Design and Product Management, working on titles of different scale for both PC and Mobile platforms.
I am a Digital Nomad - meaning, I mostly collaborate with other people remotely while travelling from one location to another. As much as it is fun, I am mostly doing it out of necessity - the rules of the modern world make it so I can't stay in one place for long.

I am mostly working on the game alone, but there are people helping me: 
All the art for crabs was done by an amazing [url=https://twitter.com/derekpxart]Derek Souza [/url]

[b]Demo Release[/b]
With this update, Crab Raid Tactics Demo goes live on Steam. I am extremely happy to be able to share my progress with everyone and get the game in the hands of players! The game participated in two Feedback Quests already, so the most annoying issues were fixed, but the game is far from done - both in terms of content and polishing. I plan to update it regularly, only including the content I want to be playtested. As soon as enough content is built and all necessary systems are in place, the game will launch in Early Access and get a price tag. For now, it is called a Demo and will remain free.


[b]State of the game[/b]
I'll reiterate on it, just to be clear: the current version is meant as a playtest material more that anything else. It is not at all indicative of what the game will become - rather, it is an invitation for those interested in the game or genre to follow the development process and influence whatever would come out of it. 

Right now, I am focused on building a Vertical Slice for the game: implementing core systems and providing enough content to playtest them. 

Currently, the game offers:
[list]
[*] Several crabs to choose from at the start of the game, each with their own abilities
[*] Basic enemy types and randomized enemy squad compositions that get more difficult with each encounter
[*] Levelling system for crabs, Upgrades pool and special Attuned abilities that introduce unique mechanics
[*] Encounter #8 is a boss fight. The boss has a number of offensive abilities that require player's reaction and quick thinking to mitigate
[/list]
